Oral Order Order No. 10 : Dated 15th January, 2021:
With consent of the parties, hearing of the matter has been done through video conferencing and there is no complaint whatsoever regarding audio and visual quality.
2. The instant Interlocutory Application has been filed by one of the CNF agents dealing with Plain Gutkha products.

3. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant has submitted that, since in order dated 12.01.2021 passed by the respondents-State, there is no ban on plain Gutkha products as such the applicant does not want to press the instant Interlocutory Application.
4. In view of submission advanced by learned counsel for the applicant, the instant Interlocutory Application is dismissed as not pressed.

5. The instant writ petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India by way of pro bono public, has been filed seeking appropriate direction upon the respondents to implement the ban on sale of products like Gutkha, Pan Masala, flavoured/scented Tobacco, Kharra and similar products containing tobacco by whatsoever name called as per notification file no. 16/KHADYA (VIVIDH)/12-06/2017/98 (16) dated 05.07.2018 issued by Government of Jharkhand, Department of Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare with further direction upon the respondents for formation of a permanent policy banning the supply, sale and production of products Gutkha, Pan Masala, flavoured/scented Tobacco, Kharra and similar products.

6. The matter was heard on several occasions by this Court and various directions have been issued directing the respondents-State of Jharkhand to answer that when tobacco and Pan Masala are being sold separately at each and every corner of the State, which is readily available at one of the shops itself, how the ban is going to Fariyaad Foundation vs Government Of Jharkhand on 15 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176021041/
2 become successful.

sentences.text: Further, this Court had observed that this ought to have come in the mind of the policy makers that regular study was to be made regarding the effect of the policy and therefore, direction was issued upon the Secretary of the department to file affidavit as to how they are going to combat the situation.

We have further observed that any policy restricting such type of sale or banning such type of sale cannot succeed unless and until, it is framed along with another policy to make the people aware regarding that, as such the State authority was directed to answer whether such type of important policy decision which are affecting the health of the people at large are being publicized properly and any awareness programme is being followed to make the people aware why they should not consume such type of Gutkha with tobacco or nicotine or magnesium carbonate?
The Principal Secretary (Health)-cum-Commissioner, Food Safety, Government of Jharkhand was also called upon in person for deliberating on the issue with a direction to apprise this Court as to what policy has been made to deal with such situation and how it proposes to fix the accountability upon erring employees/officers so as to there may not be any slackness on their part to restrict such articles from entering into each district of the State.
In pursuance to the aforesaid direction, 3rd Supplementary counter affidavit was filed by respondent no. 3- Principal Secretary (Health)-cum-Commissioner, Food Safety, Government of Jharkhand.

7. Learned counsel appearing for the respondents-State of Jharkhand has argued out the case by placing the averments made in the 3rd supplementary counter affidavit, in particular order dated 12.01.2021 issued under the Signature of Principal Secretary-cum-Commissioner of Food Safety,
Jharkhand, Annexure S to the 3rd Supplementary counter affidavit, wherein the State of Jharkhand taking into consideration various Rules and Regulations, the observations made by Hon'ble Apex Court as also the order passed by this Court in this 'Public Interest Litigation in particular order dated 16.10.2020 and 04.12.2020, at paragraph 20 of the order dated 12.01.2021 has taken following decisions:
20.In view of the above

, there is imperative need to take strict action against sale of chewing Tobacco containing food additives and sale of twin packs of Pan Masala with adulterant Chewing Tobacco (chotu), in compliance with the notifications/orders of the State of Jharkhand and directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and High Court of Jharkhand and therefore ensure the following:
(a).There is no sale of chewing tobacco products which is flavoured or scented or cloured by the use of food or food addictive such as spices, saffron kewda, menthol,
lime, water, oil etc for one year from the date of issuance of the order.

sentences.text: (c).There is no transport, storage, distribution and sale of Pan Masala and Tobacco Products without genuine e-way bills and invoices for one year from the date of issuance of the order.
(d).There is no sale of tobacco products without authorization/license issued under the Jharkhand Municipal Corporation Act, 2011 for one year from the date of issuance of the order.

Further the terms and condition of license shall also envisage that tobacco products will not be sold with food articles including Pan Masala and shall comply with the tobacco control provisions envisaged under the Cigarettes and other Tobacco products (Prohibition of Advertisment and Regulations of Trade and Commerce Production, Supply and Distribution) Act 2003 and Rules, the Juvenine Justice (Care and Protectiion of Children) Act, 2015 and the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 and its Regulations.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the State further referring to Annexure A to the 3rd Supplementary Counter affidavit has submitted that in pursuance to the order dated 04.12.2020 passed by this Court in the instant 'Public Interest Litigation' for fixing accountability for search/seizure/raid effectively, the department has directed all the Deputy Commissioners of the State of Jharkhand to identify the entry points in each district and depute an officer who will be responsible for illegal entry of prohibited pan masala and tobacco.
Pursuant thereto, all prohibitory steps have been taken in different district of the State, as would appear from Annexures B to Q to the 3 rd supplementary counter affidavit.

8. Upon this, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that although the government has made out the mechanism to effectively implement the policy decision pertaining to ban of the Gutkha etc. but the pertinent question would be how to implement it as this Court had also made reference in this regard in order dated 04.12.2020 to the effect that "strict vigilance at the entry point in each district of the State and accountability upon the officers who have been posted at entry point will not be fixed, the entire purpose of banning Gutkha/Nicotine will be frustrated", as such appropriate direction be passed since the same does not find mention in the 3rd supplementary counter affidavit.

9. Ms. Ritu Kumar, learned counsel for the intervener has placed the Intervention Petition, being I.A. No. 6024 of 2020, and has submitted that the effectiveness in implementing the ban order of State Government is of paramount consideration.
In this regard, she has furnished an example in the application and prayed that appropriate order may be passed for effective implementation of the orders passed in this regard.

sentences.text:
This Court, having heard learned counsel for the parties and after consideration of the rival submission made on their behalf and considering the relief sought for in this 'Public Interest Litigation, as also taking into consideration the approach of the government by issuing various directions as contained order dated 12.01.2021 for banning of sale of chewing Gutkha, Pan Masala,
flavoured/scented Tobacco, Kharra and similar products containing tobacco, as mentioned and quoted herein above, and further the endeavours have been taken by issuing direction to ensure compliance of the government order dated 12.01.2021, deem it fit and proper to consign the matter with direction to respondent-State of Jharkhand to ensure compliance of order dated 12.01.2021.
We further direct that the Deputy Commissioners of each and every district along with Senior Superintendent of Police/Superintendent of Police of the district shall monitor the action/duty of the authorities who have been assigned duty by virtue of various orders passed in this regard at the district level as has been annexed as Annexures B to Q to the 3 rd supplementary counter affidavit in order to fix the accountability upon the officials in case of slackness on the part of the concerned authority and to initiate appropriate proceeding, if necessary.

11. With the aforesaid observations and direction, the instant writ petition by way of 'Public Interest Litigation' is consigned with liberty to the petitioner or any of the aggrieved to approach this Court in case of any violation of order dated 12.01.2021 considering the importance of the matter since the same pertains to health of the citizens.

12. In view of the disposal of the instant writ petition, the Interlocutory Applications, being I.A. No.
6024 of 2020, I.A. No. 6138 of 2020 and I.A. No. 6077 of 2020 also stand disposed of.

(Dr. Ravi Ranjan, C.J.) (Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) Alankar/ -
